title: Gerbner–Keszegh–Methuku–Abhishek–Nagy–Patkós–Tompkins–Xiao Conjecture
statement_text: The size of pairs of set systems satisfying both the Two Families hypotheses of Bollob\'{a}s and an intersection condition on the first family is bounded by the Ahlswede-Khachatrian bound on the size of $t$-intersecting families.
context_text: Gerbner, Keszegh, Methuku, Abhishek, Nagy, Patk\'{o}s, Tompkins, and Xiao conjectured a bound for pairs of families satisfying simultaneously the Bollob\'{a}s Two Families condition and a cross-intersection condition. Section 5 of the paper is devoted to its affirmative resolution.
attributed_to: Gerbner, Keszegh, Methuku, Abhishek, Nagy, Patkós, Tompkins, and Xiao
paper_contribution: The authors affirmatively resolve the conjecture, proving that such pairs of families are bounded in size by the Ahlswede-Khachatrian bound for $t$-intersecting families.

title: Question on extremal self-annihilating subspaces (Theorem 2.3)
statement_text: For $r < n/2$, are all extremal self-annihilating subspaces $W \subseteq \bigwedge^r V$ (those with $\dim W = \binom{n-1}{r-1}$) of the form $\{v \wedge z : z \in \bigwedge^{r-1} V\}$ for some fixed $v \in V$?
context_text: Let $V=\mathbb{R}^n$ (the arguments work over any field of characteristic $0$) and let $\bigwedge^r V$ be its $r$-th exterior power, of dimension $\binom{n}{r}$, with wedge product $\wedge$. A subspace $W$ of the exterior algebra is self-annihilating if $u\wedge w=0$ for all $u,w\in W$, and two subspaces $U,W$ are mutually annihilating if $u\wedge w=0$ for all $u\in U$, $w\in W$. These are exterior analogues of intersecting and cross-intersecting families of sets: for a basis $f_1,\dots,f_n$, the monomial $f_A=f_{a_1}\wedge\dots\wedge f_{a_r}$ wedged with $f_B$ vanishes exactly when $A\cap B\ne\emptyset$. By the Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem an intersecting $r$-uniform family on $[n]$ with $r\le n/2$ has at most $\binom{n-1}{r-1}$ sets, and for $r<n/2$ the extremal families are exactly the stars (all sets containing a fixed element). The authors prove an exterior Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem: a self-annihilating subspace $W$ of $\bigwedge V$ has $\dim W\le2^{n-1}$, and if $W\subseteq\bigwedge^r V$ with $r\le n/2$ then $\dim W\le\binom{n-1}{r-1}$ (the proof shows that the initial hypergraph of $W$ with respect to a basis is intersecting; Woodroofe gave another proof). Both bounds are attained by $\{v\wedge z\}$ for a fixed $v\in V$, the analogue of a star. The authors ask whether, as for sets, these are the only extremal examples; this holds trivially for $r=1$, and also for $r=2$ since then elements of self-annihilating spaces are decomposable.
notes: Stated in running prose after Theorem 2.3: 'It is an interesting question to describe the extremal examples for Theorem 2.3 ... Could all extremal examples be of this form?' PDF source.

title: Question on extremal mutually annihilating pairs (Theorem 2.4)
statement_text: For $r, s < n/2$, characterize all pairs of subspaces $U \subseteq \bigwedge^r V$ and $W \subseteq \bigwedge^s V$ that are mutually annihilating and attain $\dim U \cdot \dim W = \binom{n-1}{r-1}\binom{n-1}{s-1}$.
context_text: Let $V=\mathbb{R}^n$ (the arguments work over any field of characteristic $0$) and let $\bigwedge^r V$ be its $r$-th exterior power, of dimension $\binom{n}{r}$, with wedge product $\wedge$. A subspace $W$ of the exterior algebra is self-annihilating if $u\wedge w=0$ for all $u,w\in W$, and two subspaces $U,W$ are mutually annihilating if $u\wedge w=0$ for all $u\in U$, $w\in W$. These are exterior analogues of intersecting and cross-intersecting families of sets: for a basis $f_1,\dots,f_n$, the monomial $f_A=f_{a_1}\wedge\dots\wedge f_{a_r}$ wedged with $f_B$ vanishes exactly when $A\cap B\ne\emptyset$. By the Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem an intersecting $r$-uniform family on $[n]$ with $r\le n/2$ has at most $\binom{n-1}{r-1}$ sets, and for $r<n/2$ the extremal families are exactly the stars (all sets containing a fixed element). The authors prove that if $1\le r,s\le n/2$, $U\subseteq\bigwedge^r V$ and $W\subseteq\bigwedge^s V$ are mutually annihilating, then $\dim U\cdot\dim W\le\binom{n-1}{r-1}\binom{n-1}{s-1}$, by reduction to the Pyber and Matsumoto–Tokushige bound for cross-intersecting families; the case $U=W$ recovers the exterior Erdős–Ko–Rado bound. Equality is attained by fixing $v\in V$ and taking $U=\{v\wedge z : z\in\bigwedge^{r-1}V\}$ and $W=\{v\wedge z : z\in\bigwedge^{s-1}V\}$. As for single self-annihilating subspaces, the authors find it interesting to characterise all extremal pairs when $r,s<n/2$.
